purpose: Document first-party local registry/map evidence and bounded anonymous parcel geometry access review.
assessment: The official municipal SIMGeo page describes the city’s georeferenced information system and public map layers. The official SIMGeo ArcGIS REST sublayer simgeo/lotes/MapServer/3 is polygon geometry, supports Query/Data, and exposes safe objectid (OID) and iq parcel-key fields. A bounded anonymous point-intersection query at the unchanged WUP point returned one polygon (objectid 94825, iq 13-20-25-19-469); an independent returnIdsOnly query returned the same single OID. The layer response flagged exceededTransferLimit even though the ID-only point result contained one OID; the point query was spatially bounded and only the safe-ID geometry response was retained. No wider coverage or runtime qualification is claimed. Exact-ID follow-up query with where=objectid=94825 returned HTTP 200 and one polygon with the same id, iq, and identical geometry as the WUP-point response; this resolves the response-completeness ambiguity for the retained feature.
registryAssessment: Joinville’s official municipal SIMGeo documents local georeferenced urban/parcel information, and the official lotes layer returned one polygon for the exact WUP point.
